facts.label: Adjusted EBITDA (company)
facts.text: EBITDA plus non-cash stock compensation, transaction expenses, restructuring, fair-value mark-up of acquired fleet sold, and other items. For 9M 2026 the add-backs are the difference between 1,538 and 1,462, which is 76 (calc). Stock compensation is a recurring cost and the fair-value mark-up is an acquisition-accounting effect; both flatter adjusted EBITDA relative to cash earnings.
facts.basis: Literal handoff table; no financial reinterpretation.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Two limits shape how far the ratios can be pushed. First, the only EBITDA that can be built for every window is the company's unadjusted EBITDA (net income plus tax, net interest, rental depreciation and non-rental depreciation and amortization). Adjusted EBITDA is printed for the 2026 quarters, 6M and 9M and their 2025 comparatives, but not for FY2025 or Q4 2025, so no trailing adjusted EBITDA exists in the pack. Second, the H&E acquisition closed on June 2, 2025, so the LTM windows to FY2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 contain months before the acquired earnings arrive while the year-end debt already funds them; their leverage is overstated against a pro forma view, and only the LTM to Q3 2026 (October 2025 to September 2026) is a clean post-acquisition window. Management's net leverage of 3.90x at Q3 2026 uses pro forma trailing adjusted EBITDA and is shown as attributed management data only. A ratio calculated here is a CP-1 calculation, not a covenant or management figure.

facts.label: Covenants and compliance
facts.text: No financial maintenance covenants apply to the ABL Credit Facility, AR Facility, Term Loan Facility or Notes. Under the ABL, "failure to maintain certain levels of liquidity" triggers a fixed charge coverage ratio of not less than 1:1 for the four most recent quarters; at September 30, 2026 "the appropriate levels of liquidity have been maintained", so the test is not applicable and the company states it was in compliance with all applicable covenants (Q3 10-Q page:33; 10-K page:115). The trigger level of liquidity or excess availability and the covenant's own definition of fixed charge coverage are not quantified in the filings, so headroom is Not calculable. The covenant definition would differ from the EBITDA used here: the ABL ratio is a fixed charge ratio on the credit agreement's own definitions, not EBITDA over cash interest. The indentures contain incurrence-type limitations on debt, restricted payments and liens, and a change of control put at 101% (10-K page:105), described at summary level only. Dividends are restricted by the debt agreements (Q3 10-Q page:33).

facts.label: Interpretation
facts.text: Leverage fell mainly because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid. Gross debt moved from 8,103 at FY2025 to 8,080 at Q3 2026 (calc), while LTM unadjusted EBITDA rose from 1,497 to 1,932 (calc) as the H&E contribution replaced pre-acquisition months in the window and the 2026 quarters grew. The mechanism is the acquisition debt carried in full against a part-year earnings base at year-end; the credit implication is that deleveraging depends on EBITDA delivery and fleet-spending discipline rather than on scheduled amortization (the term loan amortizes at 1.00% a year). The LTM to Q3 2026 window starts after the H&E closing, so the stated pro forma element should add little there. Analyst interpretation: management's lower 3.90x is therefore mostly add-backs rather than pro forma earnings; this cannot be verified without FY2025 adjusted EBITDA.

facts.label: Interpretation
facts.text: Fleet reinvestment absorbs much of the EBITDA. Net rental equipment capex was 857 over the LTM (calc) and the raised outlook of US$1,000m to US$1,100m for FY2026 against 737 in 9M 2026 implies Q4 2026 net rental capex of 263 to 363 (calc). Operating cash flow of 951 in 9M 2026 exceeded net capex and left company-defined free cash flow of 133, but derived free cash flow was negative in Q3 2026 and equipment purchases in payables rose to 252 from 19 at FY2025 (10-K page:81; Q3 10-Q page:6). The implication is that liquidity must absorb timing swings in fleet payments, and the revolver, not internally generated cash, is the buffer.

facts.label: Interpretation
facts.text: Interest is mostly fixed and lumpy by coupon dates. The five Senior Notes (4,750, fixed rate) carry coupons that sum to 318.75 a year (calc), paid on June 15 and December 15 for the 2029, 2030 and 2033 Notes and on March 15 and September 15 for the 2031 and 2034 Notes. That explains cash interest of 169 in Q2 2026 against 81 in Q3 2026 (calc). Floating debt (ABL, Term Loan, AR Facility) is 3,244 at September 30, 2026, which is 40.1% of gross debt (calc), so a change in short-term rates feeds directly into that share. Weighted stated rates at September 30, 2026 were 5.24% (ABL), 5.64% (Term Loan) and 4.49% (AR Facility) against 5.10%, 5.52% and 4.68% at December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:17; 10-K page:103), so floating costs were not lower than at year-end. Indicative annual interest at September 30, 2026 stated rates is 491.65 (calc), against LTM cash interest of 530 and Q3 2026 interest expense of 126, which brackets a run-rate near 500.

facts.label: Interpretation
facts.text: Liquidity depends on the borrowing base and a single facility. Cash plus ABL availability was 2,100 at Q3 2026, up from 1,932 at FY2025, helped by lower ABL borrowings and the replacement of 25 of bank letters of credit with surety-backed ones. The AR Facility is fully drawn and matures August 31, 2027; the company classifies it as long-term on its intent and ability to refinance it or use ABL capacity (Q3 10-Q page:18), which makes the revolver the fallback. The ABL matures June 2, 2030. No maintenance covenant restricts drawing, but a fixed charge test would apply if availability fell below an unquantified level.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The credit story is a scaled, fragmented-market equipment renter that doubled its footprint in one transaction and is now working through the leverage that transaction created. Operating facts are well documented and issuer-specific: one reportable segment, a fleet with original equipment cost of about US$10.0 billion at Q3 2026, 615 locations, a diversified end-market mix with national accounts at 49% of FY2025 rental revenue, and demand that management ties to large projects. The transaction facts are also well documented: the H&E acquisition, its funding mix, the December 2025 refinancing of the 2027 notes, the Cinelease sale and the 2026 AR Facility upsizing. Ownership is the thinnest area: the filings identify no sponsor, parent or controlling holder, but the holder detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so control and alignment are Insufficient Information rather than a conclusion.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The mechanisms that matter to a creditor are these. Rental revenue is earned on a fleet that must be continually replaced, so cash conversion is set by the gap between EBITDA and fleet spending, not by EBITDA alone (CP-1 shows EBITDA after net rental capex of US$1,075m on LTM EBITDA of US$1,932m). The acquisition was paid for mostly with new secured and unsecured debt, and the unsecured Senior Notes rank behind secured facilities that can reach a maximum of US$4,000m under the ABL plus the US$750m term loan, so the pool of assets that cover the notes depends on how much of the ABL is drawn. Management states the integration is complete and that revenue and cost synergies "are tracking to plan" (Q2 release page:1), but no synergy target or bridge is supplied, so the earnings uplift that deleveraging needs cannot be tested from the filings. Cyclical and seasonal demand, fuel and delivery cost inflation, and floating-rate exposure are the stated operating pressures.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: H&E Equipment Services, Inc. acquisition (Documentary Fact, completed). On June 2, 2025 Herc Holdings completed the acquisition of all outstanding H&E common stock under a merger agreement dated February 19, 2025, paying "$78.75 in cash and 0.1287 shares of Company common stock on a per-H&E share basis" for a total purchase price of 4.8 billion US dollars, made up of 2.9 billion in cash and about 4.7 million Herc shares valued at 584m, with a further 1.4 billion of H&E debt repaid in cash and not assumed (Q3 10-Q page:15; 10-K page:97). There is no sponsor and no seller other than H&E's public shareholders. H&E brought approximately 160 branches in over 30 states and 2,500 team members (10-K page:8, page:97). Management calls it "the largest in the history of our industry" (Q1 release page:1; Management Language, not adopted). Funding was new debt: 2.8 billion in senior unsecured notes (the 7.00% Senior Notes due 2030 at 1.65 billion and the 7.25% Senior Notes due 2033 at 1.1 billion), a 750m Term Loan Facility and 2.5 billion of borrowings under a new ABL Credit Facility, of which approximately 1.6 billion repaid the prior ABL (10-K page:97, page:57). A senior secured 364-day bridge facility of up to 4.5 billion was committed in February 2025, undrawn, and terminated after the notes, term loan and ABL were in place (10-K page:118). Transaction expenses tied to H&E were 193m in FY2025, including a 64m termination fee paid on H&E's behalf, 27m of advisory fees and 21m of bridge commitment fees (10-K page:98). The purchase price allocation recorded customer relationships of 1,190 with a ten-year life and goodwill of 2,171 after a 12m measurement-period reduction in Q2 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:15-16); the 10-K showed goodwill of 2,183 before that adjustment (logged under Conflicts). Liquidity and leverage effect: total debt as printed rose from 4,086 at December 31, 2024 to 8,047 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:103); CP-1 gross debt was 8,103 at FY2025 and 8,080 at Q3 2026 (Analyst Interpretation: the acquisition debt is carried in full against earnings that became a full-year contribution only in the LTM to Q3 2026). Integration status is Management Language: Q1 release page:1 states the company "successfully completed the integration of our H&E acquisition" and Q3 10-Q page:25 states "We have completed the integration of H&E and continue to focus on realizing the anticipated operational synergies". The synergy plan is described as running "over our three-year synergy plan" (Q1 release page:1) without a stated amount; this is Insufficient Information and is a gap, not an adverse finding.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues (Documentary Fact). On June 2, 2025 the 7.00% Senior Notes due 2030 (1.65 billion) and 7.25% Senior Notes due 2033 (1.1 billion) were issued, with the Term Loan Facility (750m, SOFR plus 1.75% after a December 2025 repricing amendment) and the new ABL (maximum 4.0 billion; matures June 2, 2030). On December 16, 2025 the company issued 600m of 5.75% Senior Notes due 2031 and 600m of 6.00% Senior Notes due 2034 and, with other borrowings, redeemed the 1.2 billion 5.50% Senior Notes due 2027 at 100.00% of principal, recording a 2m loss on extinguishment (10-K page:104, page:108, page:112). The June 7, 2024 6.625% Senior Notes due 2029 (800m) remain outstanding. Mechanism and implication: the December refinancing removed the nearest unsecured maturity and moved the next notes maturity to 2029, so the near-dated debt is the AR Facility and the revolver rather than the notes; CP-1 shows the debt maturing schedule at December 31, 2025. All notes are senior unsecured, guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries, with a change of control repurchase offer at 101% (10-K page:105); the filings describe the ABL as permitting "future secured debt on a basis either pari passu with, or subordinated to, the liens securing the New ABL Credit Facility" (10-K page:114), which is legal capacity that could dilute the unsecured notes' asset coverage; no such issuance is documented.

facts.text: Other 2025 and 2026 events (Documentary Fact). Otay Mesa Sales was acquired on July 16, 2024 for about 273m using cash and ABL drawings (10-K page:98). Cinelease was sold on July 31, 2025 for initial cash consideration of 100m plus earnouts, after a 49m pre-tax loss on assets held for sale in Q2 2025, and "the net proceeds from the sale of Cinelease" were used "to repay indebtedness" (10-K page:57, page:101); an earnout receivable of 32m is carried at fair value and depends on Cinelease revenue in 2027 and 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:22). The AR Facility was extended in August 2025 and increased from 400m to 475m in December 2025, to 500m in May 2026, and in August 2026 to 550m with maturity extended to August 31, 2027 (10-K page:57; Q3 10-Q page:18). In July 2026 the company replaced certain insurance-related bank letters of credit with surety-backed letters of credit, adding about 25m of ABL capacity (Q3 10-Q page:32). Subsequent event after the Q3 period end: on October 27, 2026 the company raised its FY2026 outlook (Q3 release page:4); no other post-quarter event is stated in the sources.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Herc Holdings is a large, well-diversified equipment renter with an adequate but thin credit profile: it is highly levered after paying for H&E mostly with debt. Its strongest support is demand spread across end markets, with national accounts at 49% of FY2025 rental revenue, no customer above 3%, USD 2,100 million of liquidity, no maintenance covenants and no Senior Notes maturing before 2029. Its weakest point is cash conversion: gross debt of USD 8,080 million is 4.18x LTM reported EBITDA but 7.52x EBITDA after net rental capex, and free cash flow turned negative in Q3 2026. What decides the outcome is whether earnings growth and synergies reduce leverage faster than fleet spending, rates and fuel costs absorb it, with the ABL borrowing base as the buffer [CP-1, CP-1A].
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

citations.quote: Herc Holdings is a large, well-diversified equipment renter with an adequate but thin credit profile: it is highly levered after paying for H&E mostly with debt. Its weakest point is cash conversion: gross debt of USD 8,080 million is 4.18x LTM reported EBITDA but 7.52x EBITDA after net rental capex, and free cash flow turned negative in Q3 2026. What decides the outcome is whether earnings growth and synergies reduce leverage faster than fleet spending, rates and fuel costs absorb it, with the ABL borrowing base as the buffer [CP-1, CP-1A].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the issuer's leverage is falling because of earnings, not repayment. Gross debt moved from USD 8,103 million at FY2025 to USD 8,080 million at Q3 2026 while LTM reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,497 million to USD 1,932 million, taking gross debt to EBITDA from 5.41x to 4.18x and net debt to EBITDA from 5.38x to 4.15x [CP-1 leverage chart]. Mechanism: the acquisition debt was carried in full against earnings that only became a full-year contribution in the LTM to Q3 2026, so the earlier ratios were inflated by the part-year earnings base and the later ratio is the first clean one. Implication: further deleveraging has to come from continued EBITDA growth or from using free cash flow to repay debt, and the filings show gross debt essentially flat so far (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, fleet reinvestment absorbs much of the earnings that leverage ratios count. Net rental equipment spending was USD 857 million over the LTM, leaving USD 1,075 million of EBITDA after fleet reinvestment, so gross debt is 7.52x that residual [CP-1 calculations]. Mechanism: rental depreciation is added back in EBITDA while the fleet must be replaced in cash. Implication: the credit's repayment capacity is set by the spread between EBITDA and fleet spending, and the raised outlook for net rental capex of USD 1,000 million to USD 1,100 million for FY2026 against USD 737 million spent in 9M 2026 implies USD 263 million to USD 363 million more in Q4 2026 (Documentary Fact for the figures, Management Language for the outlook).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, liquidity is adequate but concentrated. Cash was USD 66 million and ABL availability under the borrowing base was USD 2,034 million at Q3 2026, for USD 2,100 million, up from USD 1,932 million at FY2025; the AR Facility is fully drawn at USD 550 million and matures on August 31, 2027, within twelve months of the balance sheet date [CP-1 liquidity chart]. Mechanism: the revolver is the buffer for seasonal swings and for unpaid fleet purchases of USD 252 million. Implication: a borrowing-base shortfall would cut liquidity even without any covenant breach, because the only financial maintenance test is a springing fixed charge ratio of 1.00:1.00 whose trigger is not quantified.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Demand is diversified and project-supported (Documentary Fact): contractors, industrial, infrastructure and government, commercial facilities and other customers all contribute, national accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue and no customer exceeded 3% [CP-1A company and operating model]; this supports revenue visibility and bounds single-name loss. Liquidity is sound (Documentary Fact): USD 2,100 million at Q3 2026 with no financial maintenance covenant active and the company stating compliance [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]; this supports seasonal and capex funding without capital-market access. The nearest Senior Notes maturity is 2029 (Documentary Fact): the December 2025 refinancing redeemed the 2027 notes at par, so the 2026 to 2028 maturities in the year-end schedule are USD 26 million, USD 21 million and USD 497 million [CP-1 maturity chart; CP-1A transaction summary]; this limits refinancing pressure on the unsecured stack until 2029, subject to the AR Facility (USD 550 million, due August 31, 2027) and the ABL (due June 2, 2030). Earnings are rising (Documentary Fact): LTM reported EBITDA of USD 1,932 million against USD 1,497 million at FY2025 and a Q3 2026 dollar utilization of 43.5% (a management operating measure) [CP-1; CP-1A operating model]; this supports debt service. Capital allocation conduct is neutral to supportive (Analyst Interpretation): no repurchases in FY2025, Cinelease proceeds applied to debt and the 2027 notes refinanced at par [CP-1A governance behaviour]; this limits leakage, although the dividend continued at USD 0.70 per share each quarter.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage is high (Documentary Fact for the ratios, which are CP-1 calculations on unadjusted EBITDA): 4.18x gross and 4.15x net at Q3 2026 and USD 8,080 million of gross debt [CP-1]; this leaves limited tolerance for a downturn. Liquidity depends on one facility (Documentary Fact): ABL availability of USD 2,034 million is borrowing-base dependent and the AR Facility is fully drawn [CP-1]. Interest burden and floating-rate exposure (Documentary Fact): cash interest of USD 530 million over the LTM, cover of 3.65x and floating debt of USD 3,244 million [CP-1]; this exposes cash flow to short-term rates and the company says it is reevaluating its approach to floating-rate debt [CP-1A operating model], but no hedging program is described. Balance sheet quality (Documentary Fact): goodwill and intangible assets exceed equity, leaving tangible equity of negative USD 2,434 million [CP-1]; asset coverage rests on the fleet rather than on book equity. Structural position of the unsecured notes (Analyst Interpretation): USD 4,750 million of Senior Notes are unsecured and effectively junior to the secured ABL, term loan and AR Facility (USD 3,244 million drawn) to the extent of the value of collateral, and the ABL permits future pari passu or subordinated secured debt [CP-1 debt by instrument; CP-1A transaction summary]; no priming action is documented. Unverified management claims (Management Language): synergies tracking to plan and the 3.90x pro forma leverage, neither testable from the pack.

facts.label: Verdict consistency
facts.text: The credit synthesis rates the credit adequate, highly levered, with sound liquidity, at Medium confidence. That verdict follows from the financial base (4.18x gross leverage on unadjusted EBITDA, 7.52x after net rental capex, 3.65x cash interest cover, 2,100 of liquidity, negative Q3 2026 free cash flow) and from the business context (diversified demand, no sponsor, debt-funded acquisition). facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence to a cautious reading is management's own pro forma net leverage of 3.90x against 4.15x calculated here, and the improving trend (5.38x at FY2025 to 4.15x at Q3 2026). The LTM window to Q3 2026 starts after the H&E closing, so the stated pro forma element should add little, and the gap is likely add-backs (Analyst Interpretation, unverified). If the Q4 2025 release confirmed add-backs of that size and the synergy plan were quantified, the leverage view would improve. The opposite case is a downturn with a sequence the filings let us trace: construction or project demand slows and interest rates stay high; dollar utilization and rental rates soften first while fixed overhead stays; EBITDA falls against a debt balance that has barely moved; fleet purchases can be cut but used-fleet disposal proceeds depend on the resale market; free cash flow, already negative in Q3 2026, goes further negative and the ABL borrowing base shrinks with fleet values; liquidity then depends on the revolver while the AR Facility (due August 31, 2027) needs extension. Observable triggers: quarterly free cash flow, dollar utilization, ABL availability against the unquantified fixed charge trigger, and the AR Facility extension. No stress number is asserted.

### Financial base view

The financial base is usable with stated limitations. Every statement the module needs (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, debt note, availability table and the non-GAAP reconciliations) is present for FY2025 and for each of Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026, and the figures tie internally: the expense blocks reconcile to pretax income in each period, the three discrete quarters sum to 9M 2026, the debt instruments sum to the printed total debt, the maturity schedule sums to the FY2025 gross debt, and the ABL availability equals the US$4,000m commitment less borrowings and standby letters of credit (all in `## Calculations`). The filing perimeter is the consolidated group; the 10-Q states Holdings and Herc are substantially identical apart from the debt held at Holdings, so no separate operating-company statements are needed or supplied.

Two limits shape how far the ratios can be pushed. First, the only EBITDA that can be built for every window is the company's unadjusted EBITDA (net income plus tax, net interest, rental depreciation and non-rental depreciation and amortization). Adjusted EBITDA is printed for the 2026 quarters, 6M and 9M and their 2025 comparatives, but not for FY2025 or Q4 2025, so no trailing adjusted EBITDA exists in the pack. Second, the H&E acquisition closed on June 2, 2025, so the LTM windows to FY2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 contain months before the acquired earnings arrive while the year-end debt already funds them; their leverage is overstated against a pro forma view, and only the LTM to Q3 2026 (October 2025 to September 2026) is a clean post-acquisition window. Management's net leverage of 3.90x at Q3 2026 uses pro forma trailing adjusted EBITDA and is shown as attributed management data only. A ratio calculated here is a CP-1 calculation, not a covenant or management figure.

### Covenants and compliance

No financial maintenance covenants apply to the ABL Credit Facility, AR Facility, Term Loan Facility or Notes. Under the ABL, "failure to maintain certain levels of liquidity" triggers a fixed charge coverage ratio of not less than 1:1 for the four most recent quarters; at September 30, 2026 "the appropriate levels of liquidity have been maintained", so the test is not applicable and the company states it was in compliance with all applicable covenants (Q3 10-Q page:33; 10-K page:115). The trigger level of liquidity or excess availability and the covenant's own definition of fixed charge coverage are not quantified in the filings, so headroom is Not calculable. The covenant definition would differ from the EBITDA used here: the ABL ratio is a fixed charge ratio on the credit agreement's own definitions, not EBITDA over cash interest. The indentures contain incurrence-type limitations on debt, restricted payments and liens, and a change of control put at 101% (10-K page:105), described at summary level only. Dividends are restricted by the debt agreements (Q3 10-Q page:33).

### Interpretation

**Leverage fell mainly because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid.** Gross debt moved from 8,103 at FY2025 to 8,080 at Q3 2026 (calc), while LTM unadjusted EBITDA rose from 1,497 to 1,932 (calc) as the H&E contribution replaced pre-acquisition months in the window and the 2026 quarters grew. The mechanism is the acquisition debt carried in full against a part-year earnings base at year-end; the credit implication is that deleveraging depends on EBITDA delivery and fleet-spending discipline rather than on scheduled amortization (the term loan amortizes at 1.00% a year). The LTM to Q3 2026 window starts after the H&E closing, so the stated pro forma element should add little there. Analyst interpretation: management's lower 3.90x is therefore mostly add-backs rather than pro forma earnings; this cannot be verified without FY2025 adjusted EBITDA.

**Fleet reinvestment absorbs much of the EBITDA.** Net rental equipment capex was 857 over the LTM (calc) and the raised outlook of US$1,000m to US$1,100m for FY2026 against 737 in 9M 2026 implies Q4 2026 net rental capex of 263 to 363 (calc). Operating cash flow of 951 in 9M 2026 exceeded net capex and left company-defined free cash flow of 133, but derived free cash flow was negative in Q3 2026 and equipment purchases in payables rose to 252 from 19 at FY2025 (10-K page:81; Q3 10-Q page:6). The implication is that liquidity must absorb timing swings in fleet payments, and the revolver, not internally generated cash, is the buffer.

**Interest is mostly fixed and lumpy by coupon dates.** The five Senior Notes (4,750, fixed rate) carry coupons that sum to 318.75 a year (calc), paid on June 15 and December 15 for the 2029, 2030 and 2033 Notes and on March 15 and September 15 for the 2031 and 2034 Notes. That explains cash interest of 169 in Q2 2026 against 81 in Q3 2026 (calc). Floating debt (ABL, Term Loan, AR Facility) is 3,244 at September 30, 2026, which is 40.1% of gross debt (calc), so a change in short-term rates feeds directly into that share. Weighted stated rates at September 30, 2026 were 5.24% (ABL), 5.64% (Term Loan) and 4.49% (AR Facility) against 5.10%, 5.52% and 4.68% at December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:17; 10-K page:103), so floating costs were not lower than at year-end. Indicative annual interest at September 30, 2026 stated rates is 491.65 (calc), against LTM cash interest of 530 and Q3 2026 interest expense of 126, which brackets a run-rate near 500.

**Liquidity depends on the borrowing base and a single facility.** Cash plus ABL availability was 2,100 at Q3 2026, up from 1,932 at FY2025, helped by lower ABL borrowings and the replacement of 25 of bank letters of credit with surety-backed ones. The AR Facility is fully drawn and matures August 31, 2027; the company classifies it as long-term on its intent and ability to refinance it or use ABL capacity (Q3 10-Q page:18), which makes the revolver the fallback. The ABL matures June 2, 2030. No maintenance covenant restricts drawing, but a fixed charge test would apply if availability fell below an unquantified level.

**Balance sheet quality.** Goodwill of 2,859 and intangible assets of 1,559 exceed total equity of 1,984, so tangible equity is negative 2,434 (calc). Rental equipment, net was 6,190 against secured debt of 3,244 (ABL, Term Loan, AR Facility; ratio 1.91x, calc), but the rental equipment is also the main collateral for the ABL and Term Loan, so the unsecured Notes of 4,750 rank behind those claims on the same assets.

spans.text: ## Request
Issuer: HERC HOLDINGS INC (issuer id hri; ticker HRI), consolidated Herc Holdings Inc. and subsidiaries. As-of date and evidence cutoff: 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD.

Task: CP-1A business and transaction context, from a creditor's perspective. Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to the creditor. The three decision drivers are transaction and ownership structure, business and operating model, and credit-relevant history or change. Each material conclusion follows the chain evidence, then risk mechanic, then credit implication. Every fact row carries one of four tags: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation, or Insufficient Information. The module gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion.

Figures that come from the accepted financial handoff (CP-1) are quoted as that handoff states them, in US$ millions (US$m); they are not recalculated here except where `## Calculations` shows a new ratio. Periods use the CP-1 labels: FY2025, Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q3 2026, 9M 2026 (nine months ended September 30, 2026), and LTM to Q3 2026. Events dated after September 30, 2026 are marked as subsequent events.

Upstream handoffs used: CP-0 (source readiness: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS; carried limitations are the unsupplied proxy statement, executed legal documents, FY2025 adjusted EBITDA and pro forma leverage inputs) and CP-1 (financial base). This handoff agrees with both and corrects neither. One point CP-0 left open is resolved by reading the 10-K note: each series of Senior Notes is guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by the current and future domestic subsidiaries, with exceptions including special purpose securitization subsidiaries (10-K page:105, page:107, page:108, page:110, page:112).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Herc is a large North American equipment renter whose 2025 H&E acquisition, funded mainly with debt, lifted gross debt to US$8,080m at Q3 2026 while earnings rose; no sponsor or controlling holder is identified in the filings. | Medium | Ownership, control rights and synergy targets are not quantified in the supplied filings; the proxy statement is not supplied and market share is a management estimate. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| H&E closed on June 2, 2025 at a US$4.8 billion purchase price, funded by new notes, a term loan, ABL borrowings and US$584m of shares. | Debt-funded scale raised leverage; repayment relies on integration delivering earnings rather than on equity support. | High |
| National accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue and no customer exceeded 3%. | Longer project rentals support revenue visibility, and single-name concentration is low. | High |

| Equipment rental revenue was 89.2% of 9M 2026 revenue; sales of used fleet were 9.0%. | Earnings follow fleet on rent and rates; used-fleet sales supply cash but depend on resale markets. | Medium |

| Dividends continued at US$0.70 a quarter, no shares were repurchased in FY2025, and Cinelease sale proceeds repaid debt. | Documented actions read as neutral to supportive; the debt documents still permit restricted payments within their limits. | Medium |
| Management calls synergies on plan but supplies no quantified synergy target. | The deleveraging path rests on unquantified synergies, so monitoring needs a target and a bridge. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

The credit story is a scaled, fragmented-market equipment renter that doubled its footprint in one transaction and is now working through the leverage that transaction created. Operating facts are well documented and issuer-specific: one reportable segment, a fleet with original equipment cost of about US$10.0 billion at Q3 2026, 615 locations, a diversified end-market mix with national accounts at 49% of FY2025 rental revenue, and demand that management ties to large projects. The transaction facts are also well documented: the H&E acquisition, its funding mix, the December 2025 refinancing of the 2027 notes, the Cinelease sale and the 2026 AR Facility upsizing. Ownership is the thinnest area: the filings identify no sponsor, parent or controlling holder, but the holder detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so control and alignment are Insufficient Information rather than a conclusion.

The mechanisms that matter to a creditor are these. Rental revenue is earned on a fleet that must be continually replaced, so cash conversion is set by the gap between EBITDA and fleet spending, not by EBITDA alone (CP-1 shows EBITDA after net rental capex of US$1,075m on LTM EBITDA of US$1,932m). The acquisition was paid for mostly with new secured and unsecured debt, and the unsecured Senior Notes rank behind secured facilities that can reach a maximum of US$4,000m under the ABL plus the US$750m term loan, so the pool of assets that cover the notes depends on how much of the ABL is drawn. Management states the integration is complete and that revenue and cost synergies "are tracking to plan" (Q2 release page:1), but no synergy target or bridge is supplied, so the earnings uplift that deleveraging needs cannot be tested from the filings. Cyclical and seasonal demand, fuel and delivery cost inflation, and floating-rate exposure are the stated operating pressures.
Not asserted here: any view on sponsor behaviour (there is no sponsor), any recovery outcome, any peer comparison, or any ownership percentage.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact | Category | Evidence (locator and quote) | Risk mechanic | Credit implication |

| Business description | Full-line equipment rental supplier with 615 locations in North America at September 30, 2026; operations run through subsidiaries including Herc Rentals Inc. | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:7: "is one of the leading equipment rental suppliers with 615 locations in North America as of September 30, 2026" | Cash earnings sit in operating subsidiaries; Holdings holds the Notes, Term Loan and ABL debt | Creditors of Holdings rely on subsidiary guarantees (domestic subsidiaries guarantee the Notes) for access to operating cash |

| Country and sector | United States registrant (Delaware, Bonita Springs, Florida); locations in 46 states and five Canadian provinces at FY2025; sector label per run context (not issuer evidence): Services-Miscellaneous Equipment Rental and Leasing | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:5: "602 locations in 46 states in the United States and five provinces in Canada"; Q3 10-Q page:1 cover | Canadian operations add currency translation (accumulated other comprehensive loss) | Modest FX exposure; ABL has a Canadian borrower group |

| Revenue model | Rental and related charges dominate: equipment rental 3,307 of 3,707 total revenue in 9M 2026, sales of rental equipment 333, new equipment 38, service and other 29 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:4 income statement; share of 89.2% calculated in `## Calculations` | Revenue is earned per unit time on fleet on rent, so utilization and rates set margin | Rental revenue is the debt service base; used-fleet sales are a second cash source but vary with disposal volume (down 29 in 9M 2026) |

| End markets | FY2025 equipment rental revenue by end market: contractors 38%, industrial 25%, infrastructure and government 18%, commercial facilities 14%, other 5% | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:11: "Contractor business represented approximately 38% of our equipment rental revenue" | Mix spans construction, industrial maintenance and public spend, which cycle differently | Diversification dampens single-sector shocks; construction-linked share is still the largest |

| Customers and concentration | National accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue; no single customer exceeded 3% | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:7 and page:11: "no single customer making up more than 3% of our equipment rental revenue" | Large accounts rent for longer on large projects; loss of one is bounded | Low single-name concentration; exposure is to project cycles, not to one customer |

| Fleet | Original equipment cost of 9.5 billion US dollars at December 31, 2025 and approximately 10.0 billion at September 30, 2026; mix: aerial 26%, material handling 22%, earthmoving 13%, specialty 18%, other 21% at FY2025; average fleet age 45 months at FY2025 and 46 at Q3 2026 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:10 fleet table; Q3 release page:3: "total fleet was approximately $10.0 billion at OEC" | Fleet is the collateral for the ABL and Term Loan and the main use of cash; age and mix drive resale value | Collateral value and fleet replacement cost both scale with the fleet; specialty share fell from 23% to 18% between FY2024 and FY2025 per the table, a mix shift not explained in the text read |

| Demand drivers | Management attributes growth to "mega-project volume" and specialty expansion | Management Language | Q3 release page:1: "robust mega-project volume and double-digit expansion in our specialty solutions business" | Revenue growth depends on large project pipelines (data centers, infrastructure, manufacturing, energy per the release) | Project-led demand can be lumpy; treat as management view, not adopted |

| Pricing and utilization | Dollar utilization was 43.5% in Q3 2026 against 39.9% a year earlier; 39.8% for 9M 2026 against 38.8% | Documentary Fact (management operating measure) | Q3 release page:2: "Dollar utilization was 43.5% in the third quarter up from 39.9%" | Higher rental yield on the fleet lifts margin without more capital | A seasonal peak quarter; interim utilization is not comparable across quarters |

| Cost structure | Direct operating cost was 42.4% of equipment rental revenue in Q3 2026 against 41.6%; fuel up 21 and delivery up 10 year on year | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:27: "higher fuel and delivery expenses of $21 million and $10 million, respectively" | Fuel and delivery are variable and only partly passed through | Margin is exposed to energy prices, and the company says some costs have "less direct pass-through" (Q3 10-Q page:25) |

| Operating leverage and synergies | SG&A fell to 14.2% of equipment rental revenue in Q3 2026 from 14.8%, which the company attributes partly to acquisition cost synergies | Management Language | Q3 10-Q page:27: "including achievement of acquisition cost synergies" | Fixed overhead spread over a bigger revenue base | A quantified synergy target and bridge are not supplied; the claim cannot be tested |

| Capital spending | Rental equipment expenditures 1,056 and non-rental capital expenditures 107 in 9M 2026; outlook for net rental capex raised to US$1,000m to US$1,100m for FY2026 | Documentary Fact (outlook is Management Language) | Q3 10-Q page:6; Q3 release page:4 | Capex is discretionary at the margin, which gives a cash lever if demand weakens | Flexibility exists, but the raised outlook adds Q4 2026 cash needs (CP-1: implied 263 to 363) |

| Working capital | Receivables 929 against 769 at December 31, 2025; accounts payable 556 against 337; equipment purchases unpaid in payables 252 against 19 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:3 balance sheet and page:6; 10-K page:81 | Payables-funded fleet buys defer cash; receivables grow with revenue | Working capital absorbed cash in 9M 2026 and creates a Q4 2026 payment obligation |

| Seasonality | Demand is lower in winter months; activity is heavier in the third and fourth quarters until December | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13: "Our business is seasonal, with demand for our rental equipment tending to be lower in the winter months" | Q1 earnings and cash are seasonally weakest | Quarterly leverage and cover swing; trailing figures are the better read |

| Rate and macro exposure | Local markets "remain stable despite the impact of the elevated interest rate environment"; the company is "Reevaluating our capital allocation strategy as necessary to address exposure to floating rate debt" | Management Language | Q3 10-Q page:25 | Floating-rate debt was 3,244 at Q3 2026 per CP-1 (40.1% of gross debt) | Interest cost rises with short-term rates; no hedging program is described in the sources read |

| Market position | Management estimates about 4% market share by revenue in a fragmented industry | Management Language | 10-K page:5: "an estimated 4% market share by revenue" | Scale advantages (purchasing, density) depend on staying competitive | Estimate is unaudited and unsourced; do not rely on it for ranking |

| Labor | About 9,600 employees at FY2025, with about 620 United States and 80 Canadian employees under collective bargaining; about 10,200 per the Q3 release | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13; Q3 release page:5 | A small share of the workforce is covered (about 700 of about 9,600 employees) | Low labor concentration risk from the facts read |
### Company profile
| Item | Value | Category | Locator |
| Legal name and registrant | Herc Holdings Inc.; Delaware; Commission File Number 001-33139 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:1 |
| Headquarters | 27500 Riverview Center Blvd., Bonita Springs, Florida | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:1 |

| Holders of record | 2,256 at February 13, 2026; beneficial owners substantially greater | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:53 |
| Market value held by non-affiliates | 4.29 billion US dollars at June 28, 2025 (stale, as of the end of Q2 2025) | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:2 |

| Sponsor, parent, controlling holder | None identified in the sources read | Insufficient Information | Control and 5% holders sit in the proxy statement incorporated by reference into Part III (10-K page:2), which is not supplied; matters because control rights and alignment cannot be assessed |

| Operating subsidiaries and vehicles | Herc Rentals Inc. (operating subsidiary); Herc Receivables U.S. LLC (consolidated special-purpose entity for the AR Facility); Matthews Equipment Limited (Canadian ABL borrower) | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:7; 10-K page:114, page:117 |

| Origin | Founded in 1965; on June 30, 2016 the company, then the holding company of both equipment and vehicle rental operations (Hertz Holdings), spun off its global vehicle rental business by dividend to stockholders | Documentary Fact | Q3 release page:5; 10-K page:131 |
| Segment | One operating and reportable segment: equipment rental | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:23 |

| Footprint | 615 locations at September 30, 2026 (602 at December 31, 2025); 26 greenfield openings in 2025, 3 in Q1 2026 and 2 in Q3 2026 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:7; 10-K page:56; Q1 release page:3; Q3 release page:3 |

| Auditor | PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, auditor since 2013; audit opinions on the FY2025 financial statements and on internal control over financial reporting | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:73, page:78 |
| Credit ratings | Not supplied (context ratings blank; none found in the filings) | Insufficient Information | Matters for market access and ABL pricing; not inferred |

| Share repurchase program | Announced in March 2014 at 1.0 billion US dollars; approximately 161m available at September 30, 2026; none repurchased in FY2025 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:53; Q3 10-Q page:35 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

H&E Equipment Services, Inc. acquisition (Documentary Fact, completed). On June 2, 2025 Herc Holdings completed the acquisition of all outstanding H&E common stock under a merger agreement dated February 19, 2025, paying "$78.75 in cash and 0.1287 shares of Company common stock on a per-H&E share basis" for a total purchase price of 4.8 billion US dollars, made up of 2.9 billion in cash and about 4.7 million Herc shares valued at 584m, with a further 1.4 billion of H&E debt repaid in cash and not assumed (Q3 10-Q page:15; 10-K page:97). There is no sponsor and no seller other than H&E's public shareholders. H&E brought approximately 160 branches in over 30 states and 2,500 team members (10-K page:8, page:97). Management calls it "the largest in the history of our industry" (Q1 release page:1; Management Language, not adopted). Funding was new debt: 2.8 billion in senior unsecured notes (the 7.00% Senior Notes due 2030 at 1.65 billion and the 7.25% Senior Notes due 2033 at 1.1 billion), a 750m Term Loan Facility and 2.5 billion of borrowings under a new ABL Credit Facility, of which approximately 1.6 billion repaid the prior ABL (10-K page:97, page:57). A senior secured 364-day bridge facility of up to 4.5 billion was committed in February 2025, undrawn, and terminated after the notes, term loan and ABL were in place (10-K page:118). Transaction expenses tied to H&E were 193m in FY2025, including a 64m termination fee paid on H&E's behalf, 27m of advisory fees and 21m of bridge commitment fees (10-K page:98). The purchase price allocation recorded customer relationships of 1,190 with a ten-year life and goodwill of 2,171 after a 12m measurement-period reduction in Q2 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:15-16); the 10-K showed goodwill of 2,183 before that adjustment (logged under Conflicts). Liquidity and leverage effect: total debt as printed rose from 4,086 at December 31, 2024 to 8,047 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:103); CP-1 gross debt was 8,103 at FY2025 and 8,080 at Q3 2026 (Analyst Interpretation: the acquisition debt is carried in full against earnings that became a full-year contribution only in the LTM to Q3 2026). Integration status is Management Language: Q1 release page:1 states the company "successfully completed the integration of our H&E acquisition" and Q3 10-Q page:25 states "We have completed the integration of H&E and continue to focus on realizing the anticipated operational synergies". The synergy plan is described as running "over our three-year synergy plan" (Q1 release page:1) without a stated amount; this is Insufficient Information and is a gap, not an adverse finding.

New debt issues (Documentary Fact). On June 2, 2025 the 7.00% Senior Notes due 2030 (1.65 billion) and 7.25% Senior Notes due 2033 (1.1 billion) were issued, with the Term Loan Facility (750m, SOFR plus 1.75% after a December 2025 repricing amendment) and the new ABL (maximum 4.0 billion; matures June 2, 2030). On December 16, 2025 the company issued 600m of 5.75% Senior Notes due 2031 and 600m of 6.00% Senior Notes due 2034 and, with other borrowings, redeemed the 1.2 billion 5.50% Senior Notes due 2027 at 100.00% of principal, recording a 2m loss on extinguishment (10-K page:104, page:108, page:112). The June 7, 2024 6.625% Senior Notes due 2029 (800m) remain outstanding. Mechanism and implication: the December refinancing removed the nearest unsecured maturity and moved the next notes maturity to 2029, so the near-dated debt is the AR Facility and the revolver rather than the notes; CP-1 shows the debt maturing schedule at December 31, 2025. All notes are senior unsecured, guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries, with a change of control repurchase offer at 101% (10-K page:105); the filings describe the ABL as permitting "future secured debt on a basis either pari passu with, or subordinated to, the liens securing the New ABL Credit Facility" (10-K page:114), which is legal capacity that could dilute the unsecured notes' asset coverage; no such issuance is documented.

Other 2025 and 2026 events (Documentary Fact). Otay Mesa Sales was acquired on July 16, 2024 for about 273m using cash and ABL drawings (10-K page:98). Amounts are in US dollars (USD) millions unless a ratio is shown; periods follow the CP-1 labels (FY2025, Q1 to Q3 2026, 9M 2026, LTM to Q3 2026).
## Sources

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Herc is a large, diversified equipment renter that is highly levered after its debt-funded H&E acquisition: gross debt is USD 8,080 million, or 4.18x trailing reported EBITDA, with liquidity of USD 2,100 million. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA for FY2025 and executed legal terms are not supplied, so management's 3.90x leverage and covenant headroom cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Leverage fell from 5.41x at FY2025 to 4.18x at Q3 2026 because earnings grew, while gross debt moved only from USD 8,103 million to USD 8,080 million. | Deleveraging depends on EBITDA delivery and fleet discipline, not on debt repayment. | High |

| Net rental equipment spending of USD 857 million over the LTM left USD 1,075 million of EBITDA, which is 7.52x covered by gross debt. | Fleet capital intensity, not headline leverage, sets how fast debt can be repaid. | Medium |
| Liquidity is cash of USD 66 million plus USD 2,034 million of ABL availability; the AR Facility is fully drawn at USD 550 million. | Liquidity is adequate but rests on one borrowing base. | High |
| Cash interest over the LTM was USD 530 million, giving cover of 3.65x. | Interest absorbs a large share of EBITDA, and floating-rate debt is 40.1% of the total. | High |
| Free cash flow was negative USD 69 million in Q3 2026 and USD 252 million of fleet purchases were unpaid at quarter end. | Near-term cash calls on the revolver are likely. | Medium |
### Credit view

Herc Holdings is a large, well-diversified equipment renter with an adequate but thin credit profile: it is highly levered after paying for H&E mostly with debt. Its strongest support is demand spread across end markets, with national accounts at 49% of FY2025 rental revenue, no customer above 3%, USD 2,100 million of liquidity, no maintenance covenants and no Senior Notes maturing before 2029. Its weakest point is cash conversion: gross debt of USD 8,080 million is 4.18x LTM reported EBITDA but 7.52x EBITDA after net rental capex, and free cash flow turned negative in Q3 2026. What decides the outcome is whether earnings growth and synergies reduce leverage faster than fleet spending, rates and fuel costs absorb it, with the ABL borrowing base as the buffer [CP-1, CP-1A].
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Adequate, highly levered credit with sound liquidity; leverage is falling on earnings growth and cash conversion is the constraint | Analyst Interpretation | Medium (below High because the source-readiness view is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, the business-context view of this module is Ready with limitations, and FY2025 adjusted EBITDA and executed legal documents are Not supplied) | CP-1 leverage, cover, liquidity and cash-flow figures; CP-1A company and operating model, transaction summary and governance rows |

| Thesis: Herc's creditors are exposed to a fleet-heavy, acquisition-levered business whose diversified demand and ABL liquidity support debt service, provided EBITDA growth outpaces fleet reinvestment and floating-rate cost | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Strengths and weaknesses below |
### Key findings

First, the issuer's leverage is falling because of earnings, not repayment. Gross debt moved from USD 8,103 million at FY2025 to USD 8,080 million at Q3 2026 while LTM reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,497 million to USD 1,932 million, taking gross debt to EBITDA from 5.41x to 4.18x and net debt to EBITDA from 5.38x to 4.15x [CP-1 leverage chart]. Mechanism: the acquisition debt was carried in full against earnings that only became a full-year contribution in the LTM to Q3 2026, so the earlier ratios were inflated by the part-year earnings base and the later ratio is the first clean one. Implication: further deleveraging has to come from continued EBITDA growth or from using free cash flow to repay debt, and the filings show gross debt essentially flat so far (Analyst Interpretation).

Second, fleet reinvestment absorbs much of the earnings that leverage ratios count. Net rental equipment spending was USD 857 million over the LTM, leaving USD 1,075 million of EBITDA after fleet reinvestment, so gross debt is 7.52x that residual [CP-1 calculations]. Mechanism: rental depreciation is added back in EBITDA while the fleet must be replaced in cash. Implication: the credit's repayment capacity is set by the spread between EBITDA and fleet spending, and the raised outlook for net rental capex of USD 1,000 million to USD 1,100 million for FY2026 against USD 737 million spent in 9M 2026 implies USD 263 million to USD 363 million more in Q4 2026 (Documentary Fact for the figures, Management Language for the outlook).

Third, liquidity is adequate but concentrated. Cash was USD 66 million and ABL availability under the borrowing base was USD 2,034 million at Q3 2026, for USD 2,100 million, up from USD 1,932 million at FY2025; the AR Facility is fully drawn at USD 550 million and matures on August 31, 2027, within twelve months of the balance sheet date [CP-1 liquidity chart]. Mechanism: the revolver is the buffer for seasonal swings and for unpaid fleet purchases of USD 252 million. Implication: a borrowing-base shortfall would cut liquidity even without any covenant breach, because the only financial maintenance test is a springing fixed charge ratio of 1.00:1.00 whose trigger is not quantified.

Fourth, interest is a heavy fixed charge. Cash interest paid over the LTM was USD 530 million against EBITDA of USD 1,932 million, giving 3.65x cover; Senior Notes coupons add up to USD 318.75 million a year and floating debt of USD 3,244 million is 40.1% of gross debt [CP-1 calculations]. Mechanism: coupon dates make single quarters lumpy, with cash interest of USD 169 million in Q2 2026 and USD 81 million in Q3 2026. Implication: trailing measures are the reliable ones, and short-term rates feed directly into a large share of the debt.

Fifth, the business context lowers cyclical risk without removing it. National accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue and no customer exceeded 3%, but demand is construction-linked, seasonal and, per management, project-led [CP-1A company and operating model]. Management's own net leverage of 3.90x uses pro forma adjusted EBITDA that cannot be rebuilt from the pack, and the synergy plan has no stated amount; both are Management Language and are not adopted.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Demand is diversified and project-supported (Documentary Fact): contractors, industrial, infrastructure and government, commercial facilities and other customers all contribute, national accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue and no customer exceeded 3% [CP-1A company and operating model]; this supports revenue visibility and bounds single-name loss. Liquidity is sound (Documentary Fact): USD 2,100 million at Q3 2026 with no financial maintenance covenant active and the company stating compliance [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]; this supports seasonal and capex funding without capital-market access. The nearest Senior Notes maturity is 2029 (Documentary Fact): the December 2025 refinancing redeemed the 2027 notes at par, so the 2026 to 2028 maturities in the year-end schedule are USD 26 million, USD 21 million and USD 497 million [CP-1 maturity chart; CP-1A transaction summary]; this limits refinancing pressure on the unsecured stack until 2029, subject to the AR Facility (USD 550 million, due August 31, 2027) and the ABL (due June 2, 2030). Earnings are rising (Documentary Fact): LTM reported EBITDA of USD 1,932 million against USD 1,497 million at FY2025 and a Q3 2026 dollar utilization of 43.5% (a management operating measure) [CP-1; CP-1A operating model]; this supports debt service. Capital allocation conduct is neutral to supportive (Analyst Interpretation): no repurchases in FY2025, Cinelease proceeds applied to debt and the 2027 notes refinanced at par [CP-1A governance behaviour]; this limits leakage, although the dividend continued at USD 0.70 per share each quarter.

Weaknesses. Leverage is high (Documentary Fact for the ratios, which are CP-1 calculations on unadjusted EBITDA): 4.18x gross and 4.15x net at Q3 2026 and USD 8,080 million of gross debt [CP-1]; this leaves limited tolerance for a downturn. Fleet capital intensity is heavy (Documentary Fact): EBITDA after net rental capex of USD 1,075 million, 7.52x gross debt, and negative Q3 2026 free cash flow of USD 69 million with USD 252 million of fleet purchases unpaid [CP-1]; this slows repayment and increases revolver use. Liquidity depends on one facility (Documentary Fact): ABL availability of USD 2,034 million is borrowing-base dependent and the AR Facility is fully drawn [CP-1]. Interest burden and floating-rate exposure (Documentary Fact): cash interest of USD 530 million over the LTM, cover of 3.65x and floating debt of USD 3,244 million [CP-1]; this exposes cash flow to short-term rates and the company says it is reevaluating its approach to floating-rate debt [CP-1A operating model], but no hedging program is described. Balance sheet quality (Documentary Fact): goodwill and intangible assets exceed equity, leaving tangible equity of negative USD 2,434 million [CP-1]; asset coverage rests on the fleet rather than on book equity. Structural position of the unsecured notes (Analyst Interpretation): USD 4,750 million of Senior Notes are unsecured and effectively junior to the secured ABL, term loan and AR Facility (USD 3,244 million drawn) to the extent of the value of collateral, and the ABL permits future pari passu or subordinated secured debt [CP-1 debt by instrument; CP-1A transaction summary]; no priming action is documented. Unverified management claims (Management Language): synergies tracking to plan and the 3.90x pro forma leverage, neither testable from the pack.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Leverage stays elevated if EBITDA growth stalls | Debt is carried in full while earnings depend on construction, project and fuel-cost cycles | Weaker debt service capacity and less room for a downturn | Material |

| Fleet spending outpaces cash generation | Rental depreciation is added back in EBITDA but replacement is a cash cost; Q4 2026 net rental capex is implied at USD 263 million to USD 363 million | Free cash flow stays thin; repayment relies on the revolver | Material |

| Borrowing-base and AR Facility dependence | Liquidity is USD 2,034 million of ABL availability; the AR Facility of USD 550 million matures August 31, 2027 | A collateral or demand shock reduces liquidity without a covenant breach | Material |
| Floating-rate and interest burden | Floating debt of USD 3,244 million, cash interest of USD 530 million over the LTM | Higher rates cut cover below 3.65x | Material |
| Seasonality and cyclicality | Winter troughs and construction-linked demand; fixed overhead | Quarterly ratios swing; downturn hits rates and utilization first | Material |
| Priming or dilution of unsecured notes | Legal capacity to add secured debt; secured pool depends on ABL draws | Reduced asset coverage for the unsecured notes; none documented | Minor |
| Synergy and integration shortfall | No quantified synergy target; integration stated complete | Deleveraging path cannot be tested | Minor |
## Calculations

No new calculation. Every amount and ratio in this handoff is quoted from CP-1 (leverage, cover, liquidity, maturities, capital-intensity and interest bridges) or CP-1A (revenue mix, customer and fleet facts) as those handoffs state them; the percentages and multiples were not recomputed here and no ratio was derived from another handoff's figure.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affects | Why it matters | Action |

| FY2025 and Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA are Not supplied; management's 3.90x pro forma net leverage cannot be rebuilt | Material | Leverage view and confidence | Only unadjusted EBITDA ratios exist; the credit view is stated on that basis | Add the Q4 2025 release |

| Executed credit agreement and indentures are Not supplied; the ABL springing fixed charge trigger is not quantified | Material | Covenant headroom, priming and distribution capacity | Headroom is Not calculable; legal capacity is known only from summaries | Add the executed documents |
| Synergy amount and phasing are Not supplied | Material | Deleveraging path | The earnings uplift cannot be tested | Add the investor presentation or release detail |

| Ownership, control and board governance are Not supplied (proxy statement not in the pack) | Minor | Alignment assessment | Alignment is Insufficient Information, not a conclusion | Add the 2026 proxy statement |
| Credit ratings are Not supplied | Minor | Market access context | Funding cost and access cannot be assessed | Supply if wanted |
| Maturity schedule exists only at December 31, 2025 and does not label the AR Facility | Minor | Maturity wall | The 2027 and 2028 amounts may be misplaced | Use the FY2026 10-K |
| Floating-rate hedging is not described in the sources read | Minor | Interest sensitivity | Rate exposure may be understated or overstated | Search a later filing |

Inherited status. CP-0 rated the source set READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS; CP-1 carries that status, and CP-1A judged this module Ready with limitations, which keeps the assessment's confidence below High. No upstream module is blocked, so CP-1A rows were cited. The earlier handoffs contain no conflict that changes this view; the two small conflicts logged by CP-1A (H&E goodwill by filing date and Cinelease net proceeds) do not affect debt, liquidity or cash flow. This module neither corrects nor restates any upstream figure.

Question: does each material claim in the financial base (CP-1), business and transaction context (CP-1A) and credit synthesis (CP-2) rest on the evidence it names, and do the modules, together with the source-readiness gate (CP-0), tell one consistent story? This review opens the pinned filings and releases at the cited locators, recomputes derived figures, compares figures, periods and perimeter across the handoffs, grades the set and states whether committee use is permitted, restricted or blocked. It is independent of the analyst who wrote the earlier modules in the sense that every figure was re-derived from the sources, not read from the handoffs; it is the same session, so it is not a second reviewer.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The trace holds: the financial base, business context and credit view agree on every shared figure and rest on located filing evidence; the defects found are minor wording issues. Committee use is restricted, not blocked. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA for FY2025, executed legal documents and the proxy statement are not in the pack, so related claims trace only to filing summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Every recomputed ratio matched: gross debt to LTM EBITDA of 4.18x, cash interest cover of 3.65x and liquidity of USD 2,100 million. | Headline leverage, cover and liquidity can be used as stated, on unadjusted EBITDA. | High |

| Two explanations in the financial base were only partly supported: the coupon-date account of quarterly cash interest and the statement that floating costs were not lower than at year-end. | Neither changes a ratio; treat both as interpretation. | Medium |

| Two summary sentences in the credit synthesis were loosely worded, including a phrase that inverts the 7.52x relationship between gross debt and EBITDA after net rental capex. | Read the multiple as gross debt being 7.52x that residual. | Medium |

### Evidence trace view

The evidence trace holds with minor wording corrections. Each material claim in the financial base, business context and credit synthesis was matched to a located source span or to a recomputation from located figures, and every figure shared by the modules (gross debt, LTM EBITDA, leverage, cover, liquidity, free cash flow, capital intensity, floating share and the acquisition terms) carries the same value, period and perimeter label wherever it appears. The source-readiness gate was honoured: all seven sources are filed documents, nothing is dated after the cutoff, and the limitations it named (FY2025 adjusted EBITDA, pro forma leverage inputs, covenant triggers, executed legal documents, proxy statement) are carried by all three modules and not smoothed over. Nothing in the set overstates the evidence on the points that matter: the credit synthesis stops at Medium confidence, labels management's leverage and synergy statements as management language, and states every ratio on unadjusted EBITDA.

Five claims are only partly supported, all as wording rather than figures: the coupon-date explanation of quarterly cash interest and the sentence on floating costs in the financial base, and three phrases in the credit synthesis (an inverted multiple, an unquantified characterization of interest that its Reader summary adds beyond the body, and a mixed category tag). None changes a number, a conclusion or the committee posture. Committee use is Restricted: the set supports a credit snapshot on unadjusted reported EBITDA, but management's 3.90x pro forma leverage, springing covenant headroom, synergy realization and sponsor or control alignment are not verified and must be presented as such.

One label risk: CP-1 shows "gross debt" of 8,103 and "total debt as printed" of 8,047 for FY2025, and its leverage chart column is headed "Total debt / EBITDA" while using gross debt. The labels are explicit in CP-1's basis cells, CP-1A and CP-2 use "gross debt" and "total debt as printed" consistently, and no module mixes the two. Downstream charts should use the gross debt figure for the leverage columns.
### Input currency and scale

All three modules and CP-0 state USD and US$ millions; no source reports another currency or scale, and none mixes units. Per-share data (US$0.70 quarterly dividend) and ratios (x, %) carry their own units. Period labels (FY2025, Q1 to Q3 2026, 9M 2026, LTM to Q3 2026) are used consistently; nine-month and full-year amounts are not mixed in any sentence read.

| F6 | Minor | CP-1 | Label ambiguity | "Total debt / EBITDA" chart column uses gross debt (8,103 and 8,080), while "total debt as printed" is 8,047 and 8,031 | Use "gross debt" for the chart column | None | Open; labels in CP-1 basis cells are explicit |

No defect rises above Minor. Process note, disclosed here because the earlier handoff cannot be edited: the wording changes behind F3 to F5 were identified before the credit synthesis was submitted but were not applied to the accepted text because the edit failed to apply before submission; they are therefore corrected in this review rather than in that handoff.
### Cross-module contradictions

None found. Direction, scope, period and figures agree across the financial base, business context and credit synthesis. The two source conflicts logged in the business context (H&E goodwill 2,183 versus 2,171 across the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q, and Cinelease net proceeds 99 versus 97 inside the 10-K) were opened and confirmed; neither affects debt, liquidity or cash flow, and neither is repeated in the other modules.
### Verdict consistency

The credit synthesis rates the credit adequate, highly levered, with sound liquidity, at Medium confidence. That verdict follows from the financial base (4.18x gross leverage on unadjusted EBITDA, 7.52x after net rental capex, 3.65x cash interest cover, 2,100 of liquidity, negative Q3 2026 free cash flow) and from the business context (diversified demand, no sponsor, debt-funded acquisition). It is consistent with the business context's own note that governance behaviour is neutral to supportive. Medium confidence is the correct ceiling because the readiness gate, the business-context judgment of the synthesis and the missing adjusted EBITDA and legal documents each limit it. Committee status: Restricted (permitted for a credit snapshot on unadjusted EBITDA, with the limits listed under Gaps).
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence to a cautious reading is management's own pro forma net leverage of 3.90x against 4.15x calculated here, and the improving trend (5.38x at FY2025 to 4.15x at Q3 2026). The LTM window to Q3 2026 starts after the H&E closing, so the stated pro forma element should add little, and the gap is likely add-backs (Analyst Interpretation, unverified). If the Q4 2025 release confirmed add-backs of that size and the synergy plan were quantified, the leverage view would improve. The opposite case is a downturn with a sequence the filings let us trace: construction or project demand slows and interest rates stay high; dollar utilization and rental rates soften first while fixed overhead stays; EBITDA falls against a debt balance that has barely moved; fleet purchases can be cut but used-fleet disposal proceeds depend on the resale market; free cash flow, already negative in Q3 2026, goes further negative and the ABL borrowing base shrinks with fleet values; liquidity then depends on the revolver while the AR Facility (due August 31, 2027) needs extension. Observable triggers: quarterly free cash flow, dollar utilization, ABL availability against the unquantified fixed charge trigger, and the AR Facility extension. No stress number is asserted.

## Next module

No further analytical module follows CP-5 in this run. The run proceeds to delivery. The report should: state leverage and cover as calculations on unadjusted reported EBITDA; label management's 3.90x pro forma leverage, synergy progress, market share and "record" results as management language; use "gross debt" for the leverage columns; and carry the AR Facility maturity of August 31, 2027, the unquantified springing covenant trigger and the missing legal documents as visible limitations.
